criteria.evidence: Uses three bounded questions to establish the first learner (students or self-directed learners), the outcome (organize/find versus choose what to learn next), and first-version exclusions, without deciding the full product.

Keeps intake to three questions. Each provides two understandable alternatives plus a free-text option, a concrete example, a rationale, a proposed pick or explicit Unknown, and text explaining how to delegate or retain the choice.

Emits only decision cards. Classes, tutorials, study planning, quizzes, summaries and sharing appear as examples or exclusion choices, not approved objects, routes, screens, taxonomy or a document set.

Makes no research or market-validation claim. The outcome recommendation is grounded in the requested resource organization, the learner is explicitly unknown, and the exclusions make the next scope decision useful without a method lecture.

Uses three bounded questions to establish independent learners versus students, saving/retrieval versus a learning sequence, and explicit exclusions. These establish actor, outcome and scope while leaving product decisions open.

Keeps intake to three questions with understandable choices, concrete photography/coursework examples, a free-text alternative, recommendations or explicit Unknown, and explanatory text assigning delegation versus retained ownership.

Provides decision cards only. Articles, videos, courses, sequences, shared collections and tracking are examples or proposed exclusion options; none is presented as an approved taxonomy, product object, architecture, screen or route.

Explicitly identifies the saving/retrieval recommendation as a proposed direction, not a research finding. It makes no validation claim and offers practical outcome and scope decisions without a method lecture.
